title: [TEST] Robots Scale, Proof Varies
short_description: ASICS reports redirecting about 200 work hours a month and recovering misplaced inventory roughly 60% faster with warehouse drones. Alongside BMW's major robot supply programme and new factory trials, the results show industrial leaders where automation is delivering—and where sustained performance still needs proving. Produced with AI: Sarah and Daniel are AI-generated voices, and the research and script are written by AI from public sources.
show_notes_html:
Produced with AI: Sarah and Daniel are AI-generated voices, and the research and script are written by AI from public sources.

Automation is expanding through working warehouses, factory supply programmes, construction partnerships and supplier investment. This week, we separate operating gains from pilot results and longer-term ambitions.

In this episode

  • ASICS puts drones to work: ASICS reports roughly 60% faster recovery of misplaced inventory and about 200 monthly work hours reassigned at its Mississippi distribution centre, in a customer account published by supplier Corvus. For warehouse leaders, more frequent counting can release staff time and bring sellable stock back into reach.
  • ABB scales BMW production: ABB announced a programme supplying more than 1,700 robots for BMW body shops in Germany and China, using common controls across welding, gluing, riveting and assembly. For manufacturers, standardising controls across plants could simplify maintenance and shape future software upgrades.
  • DeepMind tests factory parts sorting: DeepMind reports 96% success in a pilot using Apptronik robots to sort automotive brackets at two Mercedes-Benz factories. For plant leaders, this is a promising step toward handling changing parts with less specialised programming, with full-shift reliability the next test.
  • MasTec expands robotic construction: MasTec and Gritt agreed to expand robotic attachments across solar projects in multiple states following active-site evaluation. For construction leaders, automating familiar machinery could ease adoption while keeping skilled crews central to execution.
  • Path funds expansion beyond welding: Path Robotics raised $300 million to expand into additional manufacturing tasks and robot formats. For manufacturers, a specialist supplier with production experience now has substantial resources to compete for adjacent factory work.
  • Beijing pairs scale with reliability: Beijing's robotics plan targets annual production capacity of 200,000 robots by 2028 alongside engineering goals including more than 2,000 hours between failures. For industrial operators, shared testing and manufacturing support could improve supplier availability and qualification costs if the plan is implemented.

The business case rests on what changes in daily operations: recovered stock, reliable output and staff time put to better use. Supply commitments, pilot results and policy targets each mark progress, but call for different operating decisions.

What we're watching

  • Path's next production task: The first non-welding process with customer-confirmed quality and throughput will show how far its manufacturing experience can carry.
